script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Family
Theme: career transition

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. KITCHEN - MORNING

JANE (30s, worn out, tired) stands in the kitchen, sipping a cup of coffee. She glances at the clock on the wall. The sun streams in through the window, casting long shadows. The smell of burnt toast wafts through the air.

JANE: (sighing) I can't do this anymore.

The door swings open and in walks JOHN (40s, supportive, caring), wearing a suit and tie, fresh from work. He sets his briefcase down on the kitchen counter.

JOHN: (concerned) What's wrong, Jane?

JANE: (tearful) I've been working in that cramped cubicle, day in and day out, for the past 10 years. And for what? A measly salary and no chance of advancement. I can't keep living like this.

JOHN: (comforting) I understand how you feel. Maybe it's time for a change, Jane. A career transition, perhaps?

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

Jane and John sit on the couch, talking.

JANE: (determined) I've been thinking about going back to school to get a degree in something I'm passionate about. Maybe graphic design or marketing.

JOHN: (smiling) That's a great idea, Jane. I'll support you every step of the way.

INT. JANE'S OFFICE - DAY

Jane sits at her desk, surrounded by stacks of paperwork. Her boss, MR. JENKINS (50s, stern, unyielding), stands behind her, looking down.

MR. JENKINS: I've noticed your performance has been slipping lately, Jane. If you don't shape up, I'll have to let you go.

JANE: (quietly) I've made a decision, Mr. Jenkins. I'm leaving to pursue a career in graphic design.

MR. JENKINS: (surprised) Leaving? With no notice?

JANE: (firm) Yes. I've enrolled in a graphic design program and I'll be starting classes next week.

MR. JENKINS: (displeased) Very well. But don't expect me to hold the door open for you.

INT. GRAPHIC DESIGN CLASSROOM - DAY

Jane sits at a desk in a bustling graphic design classroom. She looks around, taking in the sights and sounds of her new environment. The teacher, MS. WILLIAMS (30s, encouraging, inspiring), approaches her.

MS. WILLIAMS: (smiling) You look nervous. But don't be. You're going to excel in this program.

JANE: (surprised) Really?

MS. WILLIAMS: (nodding) Absolutely. You have a natural talent for design. And with hard work and dedication, you'll be creating stunning visuals in no time.

INT. KITCHEN - NIGHT

Jane and John sit at the kitchen table, surrounded by piles of graphic design books and supplies.

JOHN: (supportive) You're going to be great at this, Jane.

JANE: (smiling) I'm already starting to feel more alive than I have in years.

INT. GRAPHIC DESIGN STUDIO - DAY

Jane works on a project in a sleek, modern graphic design studio. Her colleagues, all young and vibrant, work around her. The atmosphere is creative and inspiring.

MS. WILLIAMS: (proudly) Jane, I'd like you to present your design for the new product campaign to the marketing team.

JANE: (nervously) Me?

MS. WILLIAMS: (encouraging) Yes, you. I have faith in your abilities.

INT. BOARDROOM - DAY

Jane stands in front of a group of executives, presenting her graphic design concepts for the new product campaign. She speaks confidently and passionately about her ideas. The executives listen intently, nodding in approval.

EXECUTIVE 1: (impressed) This is fantastic work, Jane. We'll be implementing your designs for the campaign.

JANE: (relieved) Thank you, I'm thrilled to have the opportunity to work on this project.

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

Jane and John sit on the couch, watching the news. A story about a violent crime in the city comes on.

JOHN: (worried) Jane, I'm glad you made the decision to change careers. It's safer than being stuck in that office.

JANE: (smiling) I'm much happier now, John. And I'm making a difference in my new career.

INT. GRAPHIC DESIGN STUDIO - DAY

Jane works on a new project, surrounded by her colleagues. She looks content and fulfilled.

FADE OUT.

END OF SCREENPLAY.
